learnings.finding: A blind text judge ranks short-form (Shorts) performance barely above chance: Spearman 0.11 overall, 0.07 for retail channels (CI includes 0), n=1172 peer Shorts.
learnings.use: Treat every idea score as a prior only; maximise diverse cheap shots on goal and let audience data pick.

learnings.finding: On long-form YouTube a text judge has real signal (Spearman 0.44, n=371 Muzzone titles); beginner framing and head-to-head titles had ~7x the channel median views.
learnings.use: For search/long-form (YouTube) beginner guides and comparisons are a good prior; do not carry title tricks over to Shorts/TikTok.

learnings.finding: Title patterns that won on long-form (для начинающих, vs/сравнение) did NOT replicate in Shorts: median relative views 1.00 and 0.99.
learnings.use: Do not assume a hook formula; test it.

learnings.finding: Plain product-name titles win on search intent (e.g. 'Fender CD 60SCE-12' 23k views) though judges under-rate them; tutorial/novelty titles were over-rated (45 гитар в одном соло: 233 views).
learnings.use: Keep a search-first content line (model names, comparisons) alongside feed content.
learnings.strength: measured (anecdotal examples within a measured set)

learnings.finding: Polished motion-graphic price slides made from catalogue photos were judged useless by the owner of MetaPrompt (looks good, says nothing a viewer cares about).
learnings.use: No idea may rest on price + product photo alone; it needs a human moment, real sound, a question answered or a story.

learnings.finding: Brand-only cymbal/drum demo clips on the Muzzone channel had a median of 390 views vs 2300 channel median (n=48); interviews 118 (n=4).
learnings.use: Product demos without a buyer question or human angle under-perform; tie demos to a buyer's question.
